newsitem.title: USA: Average NYC hotel rate rises to $160 a day - study.
newsitem.headline: Average NYC hotel rate rises to $160 a day - study.

text.p: The average cost of a hotel room in New York City rose $15.22 to $160.57 a day in 1996 as hotel occupancy rates firmed to their highest rate in 14 years, accountant Coopers & Lybrand said Monday.

Hotels look for the growth to continue at least through the first quarter of 1997, as they forecast travellers will pay $157.29 on average, $11.33 more than the year-ago period, with occupancy seen rising 2.7 percent to 74 percent.
More demand from tourists and business travellers, coupled with the lack of new hotel rooms in a city that on average has around 60,000 rooms available, has boosted how much hotels can charge.

Arthur Adler, a hotel industry consultant for Coopers & Lybrand, said, "Demand is very, very strong, both from the commercial segment as well as the leisure and international segments...The second reason is supply has been static, there's been no real increase except for a couple of hotels."

The average occupancy rate in 1996 was 83.6 percent, up from 81.3 percent the year before, with tourists the most competitive group as their rate of 87.2 percent was closely followed by those who were attending conventions at 87 percent.

The average cost of a renting a deluxe room rose to $310.07 from $290.48, with the low-end of the scale represented by tourists, who paid $89.01 on average, though that was an increase from $80.65 a year ago.
